Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. # - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.

payload.instruction: Make her close her jacket fully
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is the woman's jacket fully closed in the edited image?
node.criteria: Pass only if directly visible, reliable evidence in the edited image establishes that the jacket's front panels are brought together across the closure with no visible opening remaining. Fail only if directly visible, reliable evidence establishes that a gap remains along the front closure. Assess the edited jacket's closure state from any discernible view of the closure or panel relationship; do not require a source-to-edit width comparison. Do not treat pose, turning, flared or displaced fabric, or motion as evidence of closure or opening. Unknown if the closure state cannot be reliably assessed because it is obscured or not discernible; do not infer edited closure from the source image.
node.binding: Identify the same jacket using the source image, then assess its closure state using any directly visible, reliable evidence in the edited image. The source is for garment identification only, not evidence of edited closure. Distinguish a genuine visible gap or joined panels from fabric displaced by pose or motion; retain unknown if the closure cannot be assessed.

node_traces.evidence: The same pink jacket is identifiable, but in the edited image she is turned sideways and the front closure is not discernible. The fabric hangs displaced away from her body, which does not reliably establish whether the panels are joined or a gap remains.

d1-progress: The node is already appropriately conservative: the edited view is turned away and the jacket flares, so neither closure progress nor its remaining-open state is reliably visible. Do not force the reference “yes” or lower the evidence threshold to improve agreement; the label is aggregate and is not atomic ground truth. Keep this check limited to partial progress, distinct from full closure, and preserve unknown when the relevant change cannot be seen. For typed edits, clarify that a yes requires directly observable comparative evidence of the same jacket’s opening becoming narrower, while a no requires comparable evidence of no progress or a wider opening; pose, viewpoint, and fabric motion alone support neither. The trace is valid uncertainty with no transport, schema, or dependency failure, so investigate the image-evidence/criterion ambiguity rather than changing execution plumbing. Low coverage here is an evidence limitation, not proof that the requested edit is absent.
